title: The owner stays in control
summary: Risky actions wait for a button press from the owner.
why: Approval buttons put a person between the model and anything risky.

title: Safe by default
summary: Dangerous features start off. The shell is off until the operator turns it on.
why: A new install should not be able to run host commands.

title: Fail closed
summary: When a check cannot decide, it refuses.
why: An empty allow-list refuses everyone. A path that escapes the root counts as protected.

title: Phone first
summary: The bot is built to be used from a phone in Telegram or Discord.
why: The author has no laptop. Replies are short and split to fit message limits.

title: Honest limits
summary: The docs say what the checks cannot do.
why: Pattern checks are not a security boundary. The sandbox is not a container.

title: Keep secrets out of prompts
summary: Secrets are placeholders until the moment code runs.
why: The model sees {=NAME=}. The real value is filled in after the scan and removed from output.

title: Exact matches only
summary: Always Allow remembers one exact command, not a pattern.
why: A broad rule would approve commands nobody looked at.

title: Few tools at a time
summary: Tools are grouped and groups can be switched off.
why: Fewer tools in the prompt means fewer wrong calls and fewer tokens.

title: Survive restarts
summary: Pending approvals and settings are saved to disk.
why: A restart should not lose a waiting approval.

title: Bring your own model key
summary: The owner supplies the model key and picks the model.
why: No hosted model service is bundled.
